item.title: Kamakura Zazen Guide: Zen Meditation, Temples & Access
item.description: Kamakura is the cradle of Zen Buddhism in Japan — home to the great training monasteries of Kenchoji and Engakuji, founded in the 13th century — which makes it one of the best places for a traveller to try zazen, seated Zen meditation. Several historic temples open their halls to visitors for guided sitting sessions, where you learn the posture, breathing and stillness at the heart of Zen practice, often in a serene hall surrounded by ancient cedars.

item.title: Fukui Solo Travel Guide: Zen Meditation, Quiet Trails & Solo-Friendly Dining
item.description: There is a particular quality that the best solo travel destinations share: they reward the attention you can give them when no one else is there to require yours. Fukui Prefecture has this quality in abundance. Low on international tourism, high on substance, it offers one of Japan’s great Zen temples in Eiheiji, a coastline of genuine drama at Tojinbo, some of the most interesting urban ruins in the country at Ichijodani, and a food culture — oroshi soba, sauce katsu-don, winter crab — that translates perfectly to solo counter dining.
